name: Holland Village
summary: Walkable café strip, expat-familiar conveniences, and a soft landing for first housing searches between Dempsey and Bukit Timah.
body: Holland Village sits between Dempsey and Bukit Timah — close enough to Tanglin Trust, Chatsworth, ISS, and several clubs that arriving families treat it as a default shortlist. Lorong Mambong and Holland Avenue deliver groceries, takeaway, private GPs/dental chairs, and evening tables without a car; Holland Village MRT (Circle Line) makes CBD days workable via one transfer. Housing mixes older walk-ups, 1990s–2000s condos, and a few newer towers; large family floorplans in the core are scarce, so many households spill toward Holland Road / Buona Vista / Fourth Avenue once they outgrow a two-bed. Weekends feel social and louder on the strip; weekdays feel practical. Older stock still needs aircon / chute / mould discipline — humidity does not care that the café strip looks European. Condo visitor parking near the F&B strip fills fast on Friday nights; ask about guest lots before you host. Nightlife energy does not create a legal bubble for vapes — possession remains illegal for pass holders and visitors. Pet-friendly leases exist but are not the default; get written TA approval before assuming walk-up balconies are cat-safe. Rents price the convenience — you pay for legibility if you are new to Singapore, not for silence. Use a serviced stay nearby to test night noise before locking a 24-month lease.
watchOuts: Condo renovation / neighbour noise — MCST by-laws, not NEA for unit reno
Limited large family floorplans in the core
Humidity / mould in older walk-ups and west-facing glass
Visitor parking scarce on weekend evenings
housingMix: Condos and older walk-ups; limited landed nearby toward Bin Tong Park / Ridout.
commuteNotes: Circle Line at Holland Village; bus spines to Orchard, Buona Vista, and Dempsey.
